comments.text:
I'm in Sydney, what happened in Bondi has really shaken so many people. It's horrific and tragic, as well as surreal. Bondi Beach is emblematic of Australian culture. Many Australians go to or have very happy memories of times spent there. It was absolutely packed with people on the evening of the shooting too, not only the big first night of Hanukkah event which had so many kids activities and young families and was next to the playground, the area was packed with tourists and Sydney-siders enjoying the gorgeous summer evening, playing in the park, having BBQ's and Christmas parties and playing on the beach. Bondi Beach has always been a wonderful place to spend time with loved ones enjoying a gorgeous stretch of sand and ocean surrounded by the city. Like microcosm of Australia itself, it is a cosmopolitan melting pot of many different cultures all enjoying the place, together.
I went to donate blood the morning after to help replenish the blood supply in the hospitals across Sydney, and the lines of people hoping to give blood were wrapped around the donation centre. There were so many of us that they had to turn a good number of us away! Even though I was turned away, I was happy for it, seeing just how many people turned out. I'll be back later in the week to try my luck again.

comments.text:
Hey I live less than a mile from where the Brown Shooting happened, and I just wanna put some thoughts out there to the void

I heard an absolute storm of sirens right around sunset, I was doing work on my computer and I thought 'jesus christ wtfs going on out there'
And the sirens just didn't stop, I specifically remember hearing a bunch of siren sounds I'd never heard before. Just clocked it as kinda weird
I was still working when I got a text from my friend that Brown had a shooter. They said 3 dead 20 wounded. Locked the doors and closed all the curtains
Texted my roommates and family what I'd been told
Heart racing and fearful for a moment, turned to random livestreams for live coverage
Go back to my phone- all my friends talking about how tragic and shocking this was
I barely felt anything. Same shit different day.
Each time a mass shooting happens, on a lucky day I'm just like "Oh only 2 died that's not bad"
I was in 5th grade when Sandy Hook happened. I literally did not understand what the teacher meant while she explained it
My mom called me in tears questioning how the world got to this
I don't know what it was like before this, feeling shocked is a crock of shit
"only 2 died" starts hitting different when you walk by their execution site every week
Eventually the video came out of the shooter escaping onto Hope Street
I know that place intimately, I know it as the corner I saw some dipshit 16 year old get into a fender bender.
My friends and I are trying to make some jokes abt it together but it's all just pretty dark
They're all concerned about me, but why? I'm just in my place I'm fine.
Later in the night when my defenses went down, just sadness and hopelessness w my face in my hands. No crying tho, it's still not shocking.
They said they got the guy, then the next day NOPE wrong guy
I went out to the store today, the cashier said the FBI came through for security footage
And this whole time--helicopters circling around. News, police, FBI, whatever. The helicopters just don't stop.
The noise only stopped when they thought they got the guy, but the next morning the vultures were back up.

No one cares anymore. Providence is crying and shocked. Yet the shooting is a 70 second addition to the end of the news day. That's not a criticism of Phil or the team. Just shows how horrible the world is. Same shit different day, what a crock of shit.
